claim: Public role geometry contains 275 non-default roles and 240 traits.
caveat: Counts are public-artifact-level, not regenerated activations.

claim: Role-vector input prompts are reconstructable as 5 positive instructions x 240 shared questions per role.
caveat: Generated responses and judge filters are not public.

claim: PC1 is the strongest axis and is interpreted as convergence pressure versus degrees of freedom.
caveat: Endpoint roles are evidence, not the causal interpretation.

claim: PC2 is provisionally interpreted as situated-immediacy/formative-state versus integrated-stability.
caveat: Shapeshifter, chameleon, and elder complicate a simple reading.

claim: PC3 supports perturbation/intervention versus stabilization/repair better than moral valence alone.
caveat: Rubric scores are deterministic, not independent human ratings.

claim: Trait profiles predict persona PC coordinates strongly, but trait-only PCA does not simply replace persona PCA.
caveat: Same-space reconstruction is not a claim of psychological ontology.

claim: Prediction-improvement numbers should only be used when traceable to canonical files.
caveat: Unverified remembered numbers are excluded from canonical claims.

claim: Prompt-to-geometry forecasting is an intended-address predictor, not yet H100 response-state validation.
Cross-model topology is partially conserved, but PC2/PC3 require caveats.
caveat: Hard clusters are not universal; PC3 is weaker across models.
